arXiv:2611.10167 · new · high confidence

Linear Response for Self-Consistent Transfer Operators on Graphons

Herbert M. C. Maquera

Relevance
Equilibrium states and self-consistent transfer operators are central to the profile.
TL;DR
Weakly coupled expanding-map networks admit differentiable equilibrium response, with zero-coupling heterogeneity determined by graphon degree.
Problem
Describe how the equilibrium of a heterogeneous network responds to coupling and graphon perturbations.
Main result
For weakly coupled uniformly expanding circle maps, the authors prove Lipschitz and differentiable dependence of the unique attracting self-consistent-operator fixed point on coupling in fibrewise Sobolev scales. At zero coupling the fibre derivative is the graphon degree function times a universal local-dynamics and coupling profile. Higher perturbative coefficients are recursively defined combinations of rooted-tree homomorphism densities; only the first two are proved to be genuine asymptotic coefficients in the abstract. Graphon response and Green–Kubo expressions are also obtained; degree-proportional finite-network susceptibility is stated as a prediction.
Methods / framework
Fibrewise Sobolev scales · Rooted-tree homomorphism-density expansion
Context
Statistical response of expanding dynamics on graphons.
Subjects
math.DS · math.PR
Keywords
linear response · equilibrium states · transfer operators · graphons

arXiv abstract Original arXiv PDF

Original abstract

We develop the response theory of the equilibrium state of a large heterogeneous network of weakly coupled uniformly expanding circle maps. The thermodynamic limit of such a network is governed by a Self-Consistent Transfer Operator (STO) acting on measures fibred over a graphon , as introduced in [MPT2025]. We prove that in the weak coupling regime the unique attracting fixed point of the STO depends on the coupling strength in a Lipschitz, and then differentiable, way in a scale of fibrewise Sobolev spaces, and we derive a linear response formula. Our main result is that at zero coupling the response factorises: its derivative along the fibre equals , where is the degree function of the graphon and is a universal profile depending only on the local dynamics and on the coupling function. To first order the heterogeneity of the statistical response across the network is therefore dictated by the degree profile alone, and the finer topology is invisible; the susceptibility of a node is proportional to its degree, so hubs respond most. The topology enters at higher order through a tree expansion: the perturbative coefficients of the equilibrium, defined unconditionally by an explicit recursion, are combinations — with universal coefficient functions — of the rooted homomorphism densities of trees with edges. We prove that the first two coefficients are the genuine asymptotic ones, the second producing the mean degree of the neighbours of . We also obtain a response formula for perturbations of the graphon itself, Green–Kubo expressions for observables, and the prediction that in a finite network the linear susceptibility of a node is proportional to its normalised degree. Original abstract

We establish quenched level-2 large deviation estimates for empirical measures of measurable skew products with compact metric fibers over an invertible ergodic measure-preserving transformation on a Polish space. Our hypotheses are formulated through lower and upper energy functions, which describe the exponential decay of conditional measures of fiber Bowen balls. Under almost-sure fiber specification, we prove lower bounds for open sets. Upper bounds for closed convex sets require only the upper energy condition, and upper semicontinuity of fiber entropy removes the convexity restriction. When these hypotheses hold with a common energy function , we obtain a quenched level-2 large deviation principle with a good rate function on invariant measures with the prescribed base marginal, and otherwise. We also derive quenched level-1 large deviation principles for bounded continuous observables and a quenched Laplace principle. As an application, we consider skew products that are Anosov and topologically mixing on fibers. For Gibbs equilibrium states associated with random potentials having integrable two-sided Bowen variation, we construct bounded strictly positive common energy functions by coboundary corrections. This construction identifies the large deviation rate on invariant measures as , where denotes the fiber topological pressure.

We formulate discrete dynamics internally in the topos Cond of condensed sets. For an endomorphism , we construct orbit quotients, backward histories, preimage trees, and periodic loci as objects evaluated on profinite parameter spaces. arXiv abstract Original arXiv PDF

Original abstract

We revisit the Bendixson criterion for attractors, originally proposed by R.A. Smith for the finite-dimensional case and subsequently extended by M.Y. Li and J.S. Muldowney to Banach spaces. First, we give a concise proof of the criterion for general dynamical systems (semiflows, mappings, cocycles) in metric spaces using Čech cohomology. This approach allows for a significant weakening of previously known conditions while simultaneously resolving existing misunderstandings. Second, for compact invariant sets of semiflows that are topologically one-dimensional and possess zero first cohomology (e.g., attracting a superset with zero first cohomology), we prove that any chain recurrent point within the invariant set must be an equilibrium. In the proof, we construct a global strict Lyapunov function using Whitney-Bebutov sections. Third, we generalize and refine R.A. Smith's theorem concerning the finiteness of the set of fixed points for analytic mappings, as well as M.L. Cartwright's theorems on to almost periodic flows.

Original abstract

The Garden of Eden theorem relates surjectivity to a weak injectivity condition for cellular automata on amenable groups. Li extended the Myhill implication to expansive actions of countable amenable groups with weak specification. We consider two simultaneous relaxations: the group is replaced by a cancellative amenable semigroup, and expansiveness by m-expansiveness. The loss of ordinary expansiveness removes homoclinic rigidity, so we introduce a proximal analogue of pre-injectivity. Our main result shows that, for a surjective action of an infinite countable cancellative left-amenable semigroup on a compact metric space, m-expansiveness plus weak specification forces every continuous equivariant map injective on each proximal set to be surjective. The proof uses entropy detection at a fixed scale, a strict entropy gap from weak specification, and finite multiplicity to produce proximal pairs from uniformly close points. We also give a one-dimensional variant under shadowing and examples clarifying the assumptions.

This paper develops a systematic framework for constructing finite-energy functions on the Sierpiński gasket using Lipschitz maps and various classes of contractions. Several properties of the constructed functions are investigated, including the min–max property and bounds for their energy. Several examples of finite-energy functions, along with their graphical representations, are provided to illustrate the functions constructed using the proposed framework. It is further shown that finite energy does not necessarily imply membership in the domain of the Laplacian. The framework is then applied to a class of fractal interpolation functions on the Sierpiński gasket, for which necessary and sufficient conditions for finite energy are established under suitable contractivity assumptions.

Original abstract

We study the -intermediate dimension of the minimal set of the classical Denjoy map, an orientation-preserving diffeomorphism of the circle not conjugate to a rigid rotation. This follows on from work of Kra and Schmeling, who showed how the box and Hausdorff dimensions may differ, depending on the Diophantine properties of the rotation number. The -intermediate dimension interpolates between these two dimensions. We use the well-understood gap structure of the irrational rotation map to develop a covering strategy to get upper bounds on the lower -intermediate dimension, and use results of Banaji to show that these upper bounds are sharp for in an interval.

Original abstract

We prove a geometric and dynamical criterion excluding minimal sets contained in the regular locus of a holomorphic foliation on a compact complex surface. In particular, we prove that every Jouanolou foliation of degree at least two has no exceptional minimal set. We also give an explicit lower bound, growing linearly with the degree, for the number of singularities in every regular leaf closure of a Jouanolou foliation. This bound persists under small perturbations, as does the existence of a nonempty open saturated set whose leaves accumulate at all singularities. Under finite pullback unramified over the singular set, the bound is multiplied by the degree of the normalised component over the base leaf. Together with a general persistence theorem, this yields nonempty analytic open sets of foliations on every smooth projective surface with arbitrarily large uniform lower bounds on the number of singularities in their regular leaf closures. On double-plane K3 surfaces, we obtain foliations with ample canonical bundle and explicitly describe and count their singularities.

Original abstract

Permutation entropy, introduced by Bandt and Pompe in 2002, measures the complexity of a dynamical system through the ordinal patterns of its trajectories. Bandt, Keller and Pompe established that for measure-preserving, piecewise monotone interval maps with finitely many monotonicity intervals, the normalized order- permutation entropy converges to the Kolmogorov–Sinai entropy. Although this result has subsequently been extended to broader classes of maps, whether normalized permutation entropy always converges has remained unknown. We show that convergence can fail, and indeed that nonconvergence is generic. More precisely, for a generic continuous Lebesgue measure-preserving map , we prove that Thus, despite the generic vanishing of Kolmogorov–Sinai entropy, permutation entropy exhibits oscillations between vanishing linear growth and the maximal possible asymptotic growth. We also construct an explicit Lebesgue measure-preserving interval map with countably many monotonicity intervals for which the normalized permutation entropy has lower limit zero and upper limit infinity. This demonstrates that nonconvergence can occur even within the countably piecewise-monotone setting, beyond the scope of the convergence theorem of Gutjahr and Keller, relying on conditions concerning the lengths of the pieces.

Original abstract

Each Collatz step changes a positive integer by roughly half: odd inputs go up and even inputs go down. We vary the directions while keeping the step size. Write x=2^m k (k odd), and let S be a set of positive integers. Define T_S(x)=(3x+1)/2 if m=0, 3x/2 if m is in S, and k otherwise. The map T_S^- differs only at odd x, which it sends to (x+1)/2. The usual Collatz map is T_emptyset. Assuming the independence of 2-adic valuations along odd-to-odd steps yields random-walk models with drifts (1+rho(S))log_2(3)-2 for T_S and rho(S)log_2(3)-2 for T_S^-, where rho(S) is an explicit series. Every T_S^- is contracting; T_S is contracting exactly when rho(S)<log_3(4/3), approximately 0.2619. We prove density results, classify interval sets S, and give a criterion ensuring every T_S^- orbit reaches 1 or (2,3). For seven contracting maps T_S, three with rho(S)=1/4 just below the threshold, computations show that every n<2^34 (n<1.668*10^10 for S=1) reaches one of at most five cycles; stopping-time statistics match the model to 3-5 digits. We study branching maps, where any member of a family may be applied at each step. Boundedness of a family implies boundedness of each member; in particular, boundedness of T_emptyset,T_3 would imply that no Collatz orbit diverges. For T_emptyset,T_1, a rule depending only on x mod 32 has positive drift (10/17)log_2(9/8) for almost every 2-adic starting point. Thus almost all n have reachable sets containing values larger than n^1.05; residues modulo 2^L, L<=10, cannot prove unboundedness. Finally, we define unified maps in which valuations also determine the direction at odd inputs. The cases x=1 mod 4 govern their behavior: if they go down, every block is dominated by the corresponding Collatz map (and a census finds only the cycles (1), (2, 3) and (3, 5) with smallest element below 10^9); if they go up, the maps behave like T_S.

Original abstract

Well-calibrated forecasting for non-linear dynamical systems is essential in science and engineering applications such as fluid dynamics and weather prediction. We present a forecasting method combining probabilistic machine learning with the structured linear dynamics of Koopman mode decomposition. Within this framework, the observation, linear dynamics, and state reconstruction operators are constructed using standard machine learning architectures, producing predictive distributions via the pushforward of injected noise samples. The model is trained using a proper scoring rule, the continuous ranked probability score, to directly target calibrated, accurate forecasts. The approach is validated on two non-linear ordinary differential equation examples and two partial differential equation examples, vortex shedding and cavity flow, using both large and small, noisy datasets. Results demonstrate that known Koopman eigenfunctions and spectra can be identified and used for accurate forecasting. The model can also produce multi-modal predictive distributions, demonstrated for a trajectory initialised on the boundary between two basins of attraction. Uncertainty is captured by the sample ensemble spread, with spread–skill ratios close to one over the training horizon in several experiments, although for extended rollouts and noisy datasets, the ensemble may become under- or over-dispersed. In low-noise experiments, temporal rollout is generally accurate for at least twice the training horizon, and up to twenty times in some cases. Approximation quality is comparable to a deep ensemble approximation over the training horizon, but at a reduced computational cost and with better robustness in identifying Koopman eigenvalues.

Original abstract

Additive separation of the Hamilton-Jacobi equation depends on the Hamiltonian and on the canonical variables, and this paper introduces a five-input Poisson-bracket operator whose values on canonical pairs reproduce the Levi-Civita separability expressions. On a symplectic product structure its off-diagonal values are intrinsic, since they equal a symplectic pairing of the sector Hamiltonian fields and measure the Frobenius obstruction of a Lagrangian distribution, and their vanishing yields a local separation theorem. Because the operator is cubic in the Hamiltonian, its perturbation expansion is exact and defines a linearised separability operator and a defect functional. For Hamiltonians with a cyclic angle, the linearised operator divided by the squared rotor frequency is an angle derivative of the Melnikov integrand, so that the defect integrated along a homoclinic orbit decides the first-order splitting of the separatrix. Closed-form defects are obtained for the polar-nodal normal forms of satellite theory and, through a covariance of the operator on level sets, for Kerr geodesics. Used for coordinate selection, the defect singles out the separating focal distance of the Euler two-centre problem as its unique nondegenerate minimum, and for axisymmetric potentials it shows that the prescriptions of Sanders and Vasiliev are two weightings of the same Stäckel residual. The residual selector and Binney's shell-orbit fit improve both actions over the median prescription for 48 and 50 of 50 orbits in a flattened logarithmic potential, whereas the operator selector lowers the 90th-percentile action spread of 50 orbits in a Miyamoto-Nagai potential from 2.90% to 0.91%.

Original abstract

In this paper, we analyze a finite-lag Markov chain approximation for coarse-grained linear stochastic differential equations. The chain uses the limiting conditional transition law of the resolved variables to advance on a prescribed time grid. Its stability and statistical properties are studied, with particular attention to the role of the lag time. The chain preserves the exact equilibrium distribution and matches the autocovariance at the chosen lag, while errors at subsequent times are quantified. For a slow-fast system, the analysis relates lag selection to scale separation and dynamical accuracy. A continuous embedding of the chain enables a unified comparison with some existing continuous-time Markovian effective models based on the temporal statistics they preserve. Numerical examples illustrate the theoretical results.

Under first-order regularity and linear growth assumptions, vanishing of the Lie–Lions bracket is equivalent to commutation of global flows on finite-second-moment probability measures. Complete polynomial nonlocal fields form a Lie algebra and admit commutator and second-order Baker–Campbell–Hausdorff formulas with cubic Wasserstein remainders, controlled by the second moment uniformly in particle number. Original abstract

We study nonlocal vector fields on the space of probability measures with finite second moment. Using Lions derivatives, we define their Lie-Lions bracket, which adds to the spatial Lie bracket a correction due to the evolution of the law, and prove that its vanishing is equivalent to commutation of the global flows, under first-order regularity and linear growth assumptions. We then construct a Lie algebra of complete polynomial nonlocal fields. For this class, we establish commutator and second-order Baker-Campbell-Hausdorff formulas with cubic remainders in the Wasserstein distance , controlled by the second moment and uniform in the number of particles. The proofs rely on finite-particle realizations, which preserve the bracket and jointly determine the nonlocal field. We also obtain uniform estimates for smooth bounded kernels and a Leibniz rule for the action of polynomial fields on polynomial observables. Examples from collective dynamics show that the vanishing of the spatial bracket at a fixed law is neither necessary nor sufficient for commutation. They concern symmetries, aggregation-dependent rotation, synchronization, the transmission of a turn along a hierarchy, effective three-body interactions and occupancy-dependent circulation.

arXiv abstract Original arXiv PDF

Original abstract

The Kuramoto model is a paradigmatic model of collective synchronization in coupled oscillator systems. Although its mathematical properties have been extensively investigated, explicit phase trajectories from arbitrary initial conditions have been available only for the simplest case, N = 2. In this study, we provide a global analytical solution for the phase trajectories of the all-to-all coupled Kuramoto model with three identical oscillators (N = 3). We construct Koopman eigenfunctions from products of observables whose growth rates, weighted by the exponents, sum to a constant, and obtain a nontrivial constant of motion from the ratio of two such eigenfunctions. Using their explicit exponential time dependence, we reduce trajectory reconstruction to time-dependent quartic equations and recover the phase trajectories. The same construction also yields Koopman eigenfunctions for the Kuramoto-Sakaguchi model with arbitrary phase lag and for the N = 4 all-to-all and ring-coupled systems. These results provide a concrete example in which Koopman eigenfunctions are used not only to characterize but also to explicitly solve a widely studied nonlinear model.
